entities.summary:
Antipope Paschal III (1164-1168) was the second antipope to challenge Pope Alexander III's reign, sparking a period of papal schism in Western Christendom. Born into a clergyman family, Paschal III rose through the ranks to become Cardinal of St. Maria before his elevation to the papacy. His reign was marked by controversy and power struggles, ultimately leading to his deposition and death in 1168.

As a key figure in the medieval papacy, Paschal III's legacy continues to influence the development of Western Christianity. His actions and decisions had significant repercussions for the Catholic Church, leading to a period of fragmentation and division that would last for centuries.

The impact of Paschal III's antipapal movement can be seen in the ongoing struggle for papal authority and the eventual rise of the Avignon Papacy. His controversial reign serves as a reminder of the complex and often tumultuous nature of medieval political and religious power struggles.

Paschal III's story is also notable for the insights it provides into the inner workings of the medieval papacy, shedding light on the intrigue, politics, and personal relationships that shaped the institution during this period.

Despite the passing of centuries, Paschal III's legacy remains relevant today, offering a fascinating glimpse into the complex and often fraught history of the Catholic Church.
